introduction.situation: Psychology, neuroscience, sociology and anthropology all make claims about mind, brain and society, but at very different scales.
introduction.complication: The sources group topics by library classes and professional fields, so the same unit of claim is scattered and mixed across many headings.
introduction.question: How is everything in mind, brain and society divided?
introduction.answer: Mind, brain and society are divided by the unit a claim is about, running from mental processes through nervous systems, persons and interactions to social structures.

governing_thought: Mind, brain and society are divided by the unit a claim is about, running from mental processes through nervous systems, persons and interactions to social structures.

key_line.mece_dimension: the unit the claim is about
key_line.rank_note: Pillars run from the smallest unit that bears a mental claim to the largest pattern.

field_check.governing_thought: Mind, brain and society are divided by the unit a claim is about, running from mental processes through nervous systems, persons and interactions to social structures.
key_line: Mental processes are the unit of claim when psychology studies perception, thought, learning, emotion, awareness and the behaviour they produce.
Nervous systems are the unit of claim when science studies the brain and nerves, their parts, functions and the methods used to measure them.
Persons are the unit of claim when psychology studies the individual human being across life, personality, health, identity and the discipline itself.
Interactions are the unit of claim when studies concern how people act together in groups, work, communication, law, play and professional service.
Social structures are the unit of claim when studies concern institutions, cultures, populations, settings and society as a whole.
